title: Arryhthmia-induced cardiomyopathies (AiCM) - predictors of clinical progression
summary:
Certain heart rhythm disorders can lead to heart failure over time. One possible cause is a long-standing arrhythmia, such as atrial fibrillation. When heart failure develops as a result, this condition is called arrhythmia-induced cardiomyopathy.
This study retrospectively analyzes data from patients who had a known arrhythmia and later developed heart failure. The goal is to identify which characteristics and factors can provide early indications of whether the heart function improves with treatment. To do this, ECG, laboratory, and ultrasound findings, as well as the individual course of the disease, will be examined. The results aim to help recognize early on which patients are likely to improve and who might require more intensive treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
->Inpatient treatment for heart failure with suspected arrhythmia-induced cardiomyopathy
->Atrial fibrillation / persistent supraventricular tachycardia, frequent ventricular extrasystoles (presumably newly onset within the last 3 months)
->Left ventricular function ≤ 50% (HFrEF / HFmrEF)
Exclusion criteria:
->Age <18 years
->Special patient groups
->Chronically non-consenting patients
->Acutely non-consenting patients
->Pregnant women
